collected from multiple sources (Clickstream in JSON, Transactions in CSV). The task is to design
the Bronze layer of the Medallion Architecture to ingest and store this raw data for further
processing.
Which operation applies to the Bronze layer?
a) Ingest raw data without transformations, b) Clean and standardize raw data by removing

choices.text:
Ingest raw data without transformations,
preserving original schemas, and store in
Delta format.

Clean and standardize raw data by removing
null values and enforcing schemas.

Apply complex business logic to enrich raw
data with customer segmentation labels.

Aggregate and transform source data to
calculate daily sales performance metrics.

originalKeyText:
a) Ingest raw data without
transformations,
preserving original
schemas, and store in
Delta format.

explanations.a: Landing raw records with minimal transformation in Delta preserves source fidelity for future processing. Original schemas means retaining source fields, not a guarantee of inferred native JSON/CSV field types.
explanations.b: Dropping nulls and standardizing records are Silver quality operations, which would alter the raw landing representation.
explanations.c: Customer segmentation is business enrichment downstream of raw ingestion, rather than a Bronze landing operation.
explanations.d: Daily sales metrics are business aggregates typically materialized in Gold, not raw Bronze inputs.

A data engineer has written a function in a Databricks Notebook to calculate the population of
bacteria in a given medium. def calculate population of bacteria (intital_population, exponential
factor) return future population = intitial population ** expontential factor Analysts use this
function in the notebook and sometimes provide input arguments of the wrong data type, which
can cause errors during execution.
Which Databricks feature will help the data engineer quickly identify if an incorrect data type has
been provided as input?
a) The Spark User interface has a Debug tab b) The Databricks debugger enables

choices.text:
The Spark User interface has a Debug tab
that contains the variables used in this
session.

The Databricks debugger enables
breakpoints that will raise an error if the
wrong data type is submitted.

The Databricks debugger enables the use of
a variable explorer to see at a glance the
value of the variables.

The Data Engineer should add print
statements to determine the value of the
variable.

originalKeyText:
b) The Databricks
debugger enables
breakpoints that will
raise an error if the
wrong data type is
submitted.
issues: Official documentation conflicts with the source key; grading uses the verified answer. Original key retained for audit.

explanations.a: The Spark UI focuses on distributed execution rather than the Python debugger’s variable explorer described by this need.
explanations.b: A breakpoint pauses execution before a line; it does not automatically raise an error for a wrong argument type. This is why the supplied B key is not accepted.
explanations.c: The debugger’s variable explorer displays variable values at a breakpoint, helping identify an incorrect argument during the function call.
explanations.d: Print statements can add diagnostics, but do not provide the dedicated live variable inspection offered by the notebook debugger.

text:
A data engineer wants to create an external table in Databricks that references data stored in an
Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) location. The goal is to enable Databricks to access and query
this external data without moving it into the Databricks-managed storage.
Which step should the data engineer take to successfully create the external table?
a) Use the CREATE MANAGED TABLE statement b) CREATE UNMANAGED TABLE statement

choices.text:
Use the CREATE MANAGED TABLE statement
and specify the LOCATION clause with the
path to the external data.

CREATE UNMANAGED TABLE statement
without specifying a LOCATION clause.

Use the CREATE TABLE statement and
specify the LOCATION clause with the path
to the external data.

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement without
specifying a LOCATION clause.

originalKeyText:
c) Use the CREATE TABLE
statement and specify
the LOCATION clause
with the path to the
external data.

explanations.a: CREATE MANAGED TABLE is not the documented syntax for this external-location table, and managed storage is contrary to the scenario.
explanations.b: CREATE UNMANAGED TABLE without a location is not the documented external table syntax and does not identify the ADLS data.
explanations.c: CREATE TABLE with LOCATION declares the external storage path; required external-location permissions and credentials must also be in place.
explanations.d: An external table definition must identify the data location; omitting LOCATION does not point Databricks to the specified ADLS data.

references.title: CREATE TABLE [USING]
references.section: Parameters — LOCATION
references.support: CREATE TABLE with a LOCATION references external data at that location rather than moving it into managed table storage.

keyConcept: CREATE TABLE with a LOCATION references external data at that location rather than moving it into managed table storage.
examTip: An external table requires a declared data location and appropriate storage permissions.

A data engineer is attempting to write Python and SQL in the same command cell and is running
into an error. The engineer believed it was possible to use a Python variable in a SQL select
statement.
Why does the command fail?
a) Databricks supports language b) Databricks supports multiple languages but

choices.text:
Databricks supports language
interoperability in the same cell but only
between Scala and SQL.

Databricks supports multiple languages but
only one per notebook.
Databricks supports one language per cell.

Databricks supports language
interoperability but only if a special
character is used.

originalKeyText:
c) Databricks supports
one language per cell.

explanations.a: The documentation does not grant special same-cell interoperability only to Scala and SQL; language execution contexts remain separate.
explanations.b: A notebook can contain multiple languages in separate cells, so the restriction is not one language for the entire notebook.
explanations.c: A cell has a single language context; mixing bare Python and SQL in the same cell does not create a shared interpreter.
explanations.d: A language magic chooses that cell’s language; it does not generally make mixed Python/SQL statements and variables interoperable in the same cell.

references.section: Code languages in notebooks — Mix languages
references.support: A cell executes in one language REPL; a language magic selects the interpreter rather than mixing Python and SQL statements in one cell.

keyConcept: A cell executes in one language REPL; a language magic selects the interpreter rather than mixing Python and SQL statements in one cell.
examTip: Different languages can share external data resources, but not arbitrary variables across REPLs.

An organization needs an optimized storage layer that supports ACID transactions and schema
enforcement.
Which technology should the organization use?
a) Delta Lake b) Unity Catalog

choices.text: Delta Lake
Unity Catalog
Cloud File Storage
Data lake

originalKeyText: a) Delta Lake

explanations.a: Delta Lake extends Parquet files with a transaction log and provides ACID transactions and schema enforcement.
explanations.b: Unity Catalog is the governance layer, not the transaction/storage format that supplies the requested capabilities.
explanations.c: Cloud object storage alone does not add Delta’s table-level ACID protocol or schema enforcement.
explanations.d: A data lake describes a broader storage architecture; Delta Lake is the specific transactional storage technology named in the question.

a) CSV b) Parquet

choices.text: CSV
Parquet
JSON

originalKeyText: b) Parquet

explanations.a: CSV is not the primary physical data-file format of a Delta table.
explanations.b: The official overview states that Delta Lake extends Parquet data files with a file-based transaction log.
explanations.c: JSON can appear in transaction log metadata, but does not describe the primary table data-file format.
explanations.d: Delta is the transaction-aware table protocol, rather than the physical encoding of its main data files.

text:
A data engineer is running code in a Databricks Repo that is cloned from a central Git repository. A
colleague of the data engineer informs them that changes have been made and synced to the
central Git repository. The data engineer now needs to sync their Databricks Repo to get the
changes from the central Git repository.
Which Git operation does the data engineer need to run to accomplish this task?
a) Clone b) Pull

choices.text: Clone
Pull
Merge
Push

originalKeyText: b) Pull

explanations.a: Clone creates a new copy; this engineer already has a working checkout that needs updating.
explanations.b: Pull is the documented action to update notebooks and files from the remote repository.
explanations.c: Merge combines branches but does not alone retrieve the colleague’s remote commits into this checkout.
explanations.d: Push publishes local changes to the central remote, opposite to the required update direction.

references.title: Create and manage Git folders
references.section: Pull changes
references.support: Pull retrieves and applies central repository changes to an existing Databricks Git folder.

keyConcept: Pull retrieves and applies central repository changes to an existing Databricks Git folder.
examTip: Use Pull for central-to-local updates; Push moves changes in the other direction.
